_what: The Run, a dog park on the street, built by tools/make-the-run.py: the field and every place a dog can be in it, the porch, the toys, the treat tin and the dog telly's rack. Ryan Boren's brief, 2026-10-05: an outdoor dog park on the street with a covered porch, swings, rocking chairs and plush dog beds; a row of trees for shade and peeing on; an open grassy area for playing fetch; and the dogs from the rescue shelter out for exercise, met the way the cats are met at Pekoe and Purrs. The dogs are Rescue A Dog's and this file never names one: roam.js reads the shelter's own list every time the room opens.
_spots: Every place a dog can be, with where it is in words, because the picture is aria-hidden and a dog somewhere nobody can be told about is not there for everybody. x and y are the dog's feet, on the 1200 by 660 drawing. A kind says what sort of place it is and a level says which part of the Run, and the moods below choose by those and nothing else. 'beside' is kept for the dog you ask to come and sit with you, so no other dog is ever put there.

_videos: Ryan's pick of television made for dogs, of 2026-10-05, in his order, for the dog telly on the porch. Every one was asked of its own watch page on 2026-10-05: all OK and embeddable, and the runtime is that page's own lengthSeconds. Dog TV King's is a live stream, so it has no runtime and says it runs until you close it, the Jungle Room's rule for a live camera; make-the-run.py refuses a runtime on it and refuses a video without one. The titles are the channels' own and are not swept: what they say a film does for a dog is theirs to say, and nothing of ours on the page says it.

_sources: Everything the room says about what a dog sees was read on these pages on 2026-10-05, and the liner notes are written from this list. The blue ball is the researcher's own advice, given to the press, and not a finding of the paper: the room says so.

dichromat.title: Color vision in the dog
dichromat.by: Jay Neitz, Timothy Geist and Gerald H. Jacobs, Visual Neuroscience 3(2):119–125, 1989
dichromat.for: Dogs have two kinds of cone in the eye where most people have three, so they see in blues and yellows

redgreen.title: Are dogs red–green colour blind?
redgreen.by: Marcello Siniscalchi, Serenella d’Ingeo, Serena Fornelli and Angelo Quaranta, Royal Society Open Science 4(11):170869, 2017
redgreen.for: That a dog cannot tell red from green, tested with dogs rather than with their eyes

seeing.title: Can Dogs See Colors?
seeing.for: What the colours come out as: green, yellow and orange all yellowish, blue and violet blue, blue-green grey, red a very dark brownish grey

ball.title: Doggone: Your Best Friend Is Red-Green Colorblind
ball.for: The blue ball: Marcello Siniscalchi, the study’s lead researcher, telling the press to throw a blue ball rather than a red one on green grass
